From playtest 0001 (`docs/playtest/0001-commander-seat.md`, response in `docs/playtest/0001-response.md`). Filed `ready-for-human` because the fix changes what the Observation carries, which both Commanders read — the opening step is a decision, not code.

## What happened

Verbatim, from the seat:

> Separately, I can't see markers for squads 2 and 3. I think they were killed, but I have not in-game feedback to confirm that. I can still tab through all three.

They were not killed. Checked against the wire while he was still sitting there: `WEST-1`, `WEST-2` and `WEST-3` were all alive at `size: 8`, each with `at: ""`.

And the follow-up recommendation:

> Recommendation: always paint own squad markers on the map even if they're not an an Objective or Base.

## Why the marker is absent

`cti_fnc_mapRender` draws a Squad marker at `[at] call cti_fnc_placePosition`, and skips the Squad entirely when that returns `[]`. `observation.SquadView.at` is documented as "an Objective id, a Base id, or empty for open ground between them" — so a Squad is only ever drawn while it is standing in a Place, and disappears for the whole march between two.

The consequence is worse than a missing marker. A Squad marching, a Squad pinned in open ground, and a Squad wiped to the last man are all *the same picture*: absent from the map and still present in the `Tab` cycle. The Commander has no way to tell which, and the one that matters most is the one he cannot see.

## Why this is a decision and not a patch

The client cannot fix it: there is no position on the wire to paint. `SquadView` would have to carry a real position for a Commander's own Squads, which moves ADR-0012's projection and the Observation document together.

The fog rule is not the obstacle. A Commander knowing where his own Squads are is not enemy intelligence, and both Commanders would receive the same new field, so the symmetry ADR-0012 protects survives — Contacts stay Place-grained, which is what the fog rule is actually about. But it is still a change to the contract both Commanders are built from, so it wants a decision recorded before anyone writes SQF.

## Questions the decision has to answer

- Does `SquadView` gain a position alongside `at`, or does `at` stop being Place-grained?
- Does the AI planner read it? It currently reasons in Places; a position it ignores is dead weight on every Observation, and one it reads is a planner change.
- What is the update rate? The picture rides the 5 s report, so a marching marker is up to five seconds behind — acceptable for a Squad on foot, and worth stating rather than discovering.
- Does a wiped Squad leave the `Tab` cycle, and does something say so? That part may be separable from the position work, and overlaps the notification issue filed from the same session.
